findings.title: The degraded-parse notice is applied to the wrong state
findings.description: D6 treats `fallback_used` as equivalent to “findings were not parsed” and directs the renderer to show that notice whenever `fallback_used` is set. The established contract is broader: `fallback_used` also covers a missing summary where findings were parsed and the verdict was derived. In that state, the proposed notice would falsely claim that no findings could be extracted; prepending the synthetic finding makes the contradiction worse. D6’s cited PASS-with-fallback-but-no-findings case is also not the normal parser state for PASS. Preserve distinct facts—such as original finding count and verdict provenance—and select the notice and its wording from those facts.
findings.location: project-documents/user/slices/927-slice.review-artifacts-state-what-happened-diff-truncation-and-the-model-that-answered.md#D6 — A synthetic finding must not hide a degraded parse

findings.title: The synthetic finding can misattribute a derived PASS to the model
findings.description: D4 applies to every `PASS` and its synthetic finding states that “the model’s own verdict was PASS,” while Technical Scope describes the input as a “stated PASS.” A PASS can instead be derived after a summary parse loss. In that case no model-stated PASS exists, and replacing `verdict_source` with `IMPOSED` removes the only remaining indication that the original PASS was derived. The coverage cap can still apply, but the artifact must describe the original verdict accurately—for example, as a derived or recovered PASS—and preserve that provenance in the digest or finding text.

findings.title: A successful tool call is not evidence that the omitted diff was read
findings.description: The parent slice plan permits an unchanged verdict when the model “did read files,” but D4 uses any successful aggregate tool call as that condition. A successful `Glob`, `Grep`, or `Read` of an unrelated file does not establish that the omitted diff was reviewed, and the available telemetry does not record which tool ran or what it inspected. Consequently, the design’s central guarantee that PASS means the model saw the whole diff or read files with its tools is not actually established. The coverage rule should use evidence of successful relevant file reads, or the artifact guarantee and rule must be weakened accordingly.

findings.title: The unreported-model fallback contradicts the consumed aiModel contract
findings.description: D11 keeps the requested id in `aiModel` when the provider reports no answering model, with the “not reported” caveat appearing only in the body’s Run Digest. Frontmatter is the machine-consumed artifact contract, and metrology reads `aiModel` directly; JSON consumers can distinguish the empty `answering_models` list, but frontmatter consumers cannot. Such runs therefore continue to be pooled under the requested identity, which does not satisfy Part C’s goal of recording the model that answered. The artifact needs a machine-visible “not reported” state or an always-present requested/answering representation; using `requestedModel` for this would conflict with its reserved substitution-only meaning.
